newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson could open capital - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson could open capital - Le Monde.

text.p: The French government plans to open up the capital of Franco-Italian semiconductor maker SGS-Thomson to new industrial partners, newspaper Le Monde reported on Thursday.

"The French authorities envisage bringing additional industrial partners into the capital of SGS-Thomson," the report said. It added that industry minister Franck Borotra recently told SGS chairman Pasquale Pistorio of the plan and would discuss it with his Italian counterpart soon in Rome.
Bringing in new partners would cut the stakes held by two big French shareholders, CEA-Industrie and France Telecom.
Nuclear energy grouping CEA currently owns 8.75 percent and France Telecom owns 8.65 percent of SGS.
CEA was intended as a short term financial partner and France Telecom, which is being prepared for privatisation, will want to concentrate its investments in core activities.
A number of SGS shareholder agreements fall due this year which would, in any case, change its ownership, it said.
As part of a 1992 agreement, defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF will be free from April 1 to sell its 17.3 percent stake in SGS, valued at five billion francs, it said.
Such a sale was highly likely in view of Thomson-CSF's expected privatisation, it said.
If Thomson does not sell in April, CEA and France Telecom could force Thomson to sell its holding to them from October 1.
The two companies are expected to sell the shares bought from Thomson on the stock market, the report said.

The entry of new partners would inject fresh capital into SGS which needs to invest heavily in research and development. In 1995, it spent $1 billion in productive investment, or 28 percent of sales, and a similar amount was spent last year, it said.

The report did not name potential partners but added that if SGS's autonomy were threatened by new industrial partners, some of the state-controlled holding of 70 percent could be floated on the stock market. Some 30 percent of SGS is currently on the market.
